title: Tetanus booster (Td)
what: A vaccine shot against tetanus, usually combined with diphtheria. Adults repeat it about every 10 years.
why: As planned every 10 years, and after wounds or bites if your last shot was long ago.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: When you last had a tetanus shot
If you are ill now or have a fever

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The planned shot is given when you are well.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Find your vaccination certificate. It shows when a booster is due.

prepare.title: After an injury
prepare.text: With a wound or bite, do not wait for the planned date. Go to an urgent care clinic.

steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in your documents
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Often soreness and a firm spot at the site for 1 to 3 days
Sometimes tiredness or a mild fever
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
Do not rub the injection site
The next planned booster is usually in 10 years
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services

faq.q: Do I need a shot if I cut myself?
faq.a: If your last shot was long ago or you do not remember, go to an urgent care clinic. The doctor will decide what is needed.

faq.q: Why does my arm hurt so much after the shot?
faq.a: It is a common reaction to this vaccine. It usually passes in a few days.

reminders.text: Tetanus booster tomorrow. Bring your vaccination certificate.
